title: 相序指示器：中性点位移的应用
statement: 相序指示器由一个电容和两只相同的白炽灯接成星形（无中线）构成。把它接到相电压 220 V、50 Hz 的对称三相电源上，电容接 A 相，两灯分别接 B、C 相；灯的电阻 R = 100 Ω，电容 C = 1/(100π × 100) F ≈ 31.83 µF，使 1/(ωC) = R = 100 Ω。电源正序，V̇_A = 220∠0° V。
求中性点位移电压 V_{N'N} 以及两灯的电压 V_{BN'}、V_{CN'}（均为有效值），并说明如何用它判断相序。

questions.ask: 如果事先不知道相序，把电容所接的一相定为 A 相，那么：
choices: 灯较亮的一相是 B 相（滞后 A 相 120°），灯较暗的一相是 C 相
灯较暗的一相是 B 相，灯较亮的一相是 C 相
两灯一样亮，无法判断相序
两灯都不亮，电容把电路短路了
choiceExplain: 亮暗弄反了：对照前面算出的 V_{BN'} 与 V_{CN'}，电压高的那一相灯更亮。
电容使三相负载不对称，中性点位移，两灯电压分别约为 1.5V_p 和 0.4V_p，亮度明显不同。
电容的容抗 1/(ωC) = 100 Ω，不是短路；它只是让中性点偏移，两灯中都有电流。
questions.explain: 由上面的计算，正序时紧跟在电容相后面的那一相（B 相）的灯电压约 1.5V_p，灯很亮；另一相只有约 0.4V_p，灯很暗。所以“电容为 A，亮灯为 B，暗灯为 C”。

hints: 没有中线，负载又不对称：以 N 为参考点，对 N' 用弥尔曼定理。
利用 1/(ωC) = R，把各支路导纳都写成 G 的倍数：Y_A = jG，Y_B = Y_C = G，并用 V̇_B + V̇_C = −V̇_A 化简。
求出 V̇_{N'N} 后，两灯电压分别为 V̇_B − V̇_{N'N} 和 V̇_C − V̇_{N'N}。

en.title: Phase-sequence indicator: an application of neutral shift
statement: A phase-sequence indicator is a capacitor and two identical incandescent lamps connected in wye (no neutral). It is connected to a balanced three-phase source of 220 V phase voltage at 50 Hz: the capacitor to phase A, the lamps to phases B and C. Each lamp has R = 100 Ω and the capacitor is C = 1/(100π × 100) F ≈ 31.83 µF, so that 1/(ωC) = R = 100 Ω. The source is positive sequence with V̇_A = 220∠0° V.
Find the neutral-displacement voltage V_{N'N} and the lamp voltages V_{BN'} and V_{CN'} (all rms), and explain how this identifies the phase sequence.

questions.ask: Voltage across the phase-B lamp, V_{BN'} = ?
Voltage across the phase-C lamp, V_{CN'} = ?
If the sequence is unknown and the phase with the capacitor is called A, then:
choices: The brighter lamp is on phase B (lagging A by 120°) and the dimmer lamp is on phase C
The dimmer lamp is on phase B and the brighter one on phase C
Both lamps are equally bright, so the sequence cannot be determined
Neither lamp lights, because the capacitor shorts the circuit
choiceExplain: Bright and dim are swapped: compare V_{BN'} and V_{CN'} found above — the lamp with the higher voltage is the brighter one.
The capacitor makes the load unbalanced and shifts the neutral, so the two lamps get about 1.5V_p and 0.4V_p — clearly different brightness.
The capacitor's reactance 1/(ωC) = 100 Ω is not a short; it only shifts the neutral point, and both lamps carry current.
questions.explain: From the calculation, in positive sequence the phase right after the capacitor phase (B) gets about 1.5V_p and its lamp is bright, while the other gets only about 0.4V_p and is dim. Hence “capacitor = A, bright lamp = B, dim lamp = C”.

hints: There is no neutral and the load is unbalanced: take N as reference and use Millman's theorem at N'.
Use 1/(ωC) = R to write every admittance as a multiple of G: Y_A = jG, Y_B = Y_C = G, and simplify with V̇_B + V̇_C = −V̇_A.
With V̇_{N'N} known, the lamp voltages are V̇_B − V̇_{N'N} and V̇_C − V̇_{N'N}.
solution: **4. Compare powers.** P_B = 329.2²/100 ≈ 1084 W, P_C = 88.2²/100 ≈ 78 W: lamp B is far brighter than lamp C.

**5. Reading the sequence.** Call the capacitor's phase A; the brighter lamp is on B and the dimmer on C. Check: İ_A = jG(V̇_A − V̇_{N'N}) = 2.95∠63.4° A and İ_B + İ_C = (V̇_{BN'} + V̇_{CN'})/R = 220 × (−0.6 − j1.2)/100 = 2.95∠−116.6° A; they sum to zero ✓.
